#!/bin/bash

# Weekly Docker Cleanup Script
# This script removes unused Docker containers, images, volumes, and networks

LOG_FILE="/var/log/docker_cleanup.log"

# Function to log messages
log_message() {
    echo "$(date): $1" >> $LOG_FILE
}

log_message "Starting weekly Docker cleanup"

# Remove stopped containers
log_message "Removing stopped containers"
docker container prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

# Remove unused images
log_message "Removing unused images"
docker image prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

# Remove unused volumes
log_message "Removing unused volumes"
docker volume prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

# Remove unused networks
log_message "Removing unused networks"
docker network prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

log_message "Weekly Docker cleanup completed"

#!/bin/bash

# Weekly Docker Cleanup Script
# This script removes unused Docker containers, images, volumes, and networks

LOG_FILE="/tmp/docker_cleanup.log"

# Function to log messages
log_message() {
    echo "$(date): $1" >> $LOG_FILE
}

log_message "Starting weekly Docker cleanup"

# Remove stopped containers
log_message "Removing stopped containers"
docker container prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

# Remove unused images
log_message "Removing unused images"
docker image prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

# Remove unused volumes
log_message "Removing unused volumes"
docker volume prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

# Remove unused networks
log_message "Removing unused networks"
docker network prune -f >> $LOG_FILE 2>&1

log_message "Weekly Docker cleanup completed"

#!/bin/bash

# Script to set up weekly Docker cleanup cron job

# Add the cron job to run every Sunday at 2 AM
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "0 2 * * 0 /tmp/docker_weekly_cleanup.sh") | crontab -

echo "Weekly Docker cleanup cron job has been set up to run every Sunday at 2 AM"

# Docker Weekly Cleanup Setup

This document explains how to set up a weekly cron job to clean up unused Docker containers, images, volumes, and networks.

## Files Created

1. `/tmp/docker_weekly_cleanup.sh` - The cleanup script
2. `/tmp/setup_docker_cleanup_cron.sh` - Script to set up the cron job

## Setup Instructions

1. Make the scripts executable:
   ```
   chmod +x /tmp/docker_weekly_cleanup.sh
   chmod +x /tmp/setup_docker_cleanup_cron.sh
   ```

2. Run the setup script to add the cron job:
   ```
   /tmp/setup_docker_cleanup_cron.sh
   ```

## What the Cleanup Script Does

The cleanup script will:
- Remove stopped containers
- Remove unused images
- Remove unused volumes
- Remove unused networks

## Cron Job Schedule

The cron job is scheduled to run every Sunday at 2 AM:
```
0 2 * * 0 /tmp/docker_weekly_cleanup.sh
```

## Log File

The script logs its activities to `/tmp/docker_cleanup.log`.

## Manual Execution

You can manually run the cleanup script at any time:
```
/tmp/docker_weekly_cleanup.sh
```

# This script sets up everything needed for weekly Docker cleanup

echo "Setting up Docker weekly cleanup system..."

# Make the cleanup script executable

# Make the setup script executable

# Run the setup script to add the cron job
echo "Setting up cron job..."
/tmp/setup_docker_cleanup_cron.sh

# Verify the cron job was added
echo "Verifying cron job..."
crontab -l

echo "Setup complete!"
echo "Check /tmp/DOCKER_CLEANUP_README.md for more information."
